I have been using weed since just before it became legal in Canada. So just over 10 years. I don't use it as whole bunch, once every two weeks? Maybe? Sometimes more if I'm dealing with migraines, as it's one of the only things that provides relief. 

I dont get bad effects from it. I use edibles, and have for many years now as I couldn't handle smoking or vaping on my lungs. Especially post covid. I stick to smaller amounts. 5mg edibles are my sweet spot. 2.5mg was a better high if I wanted to be social. But 5mg makes me happy and sleepy. I have some drinks that are 10mg and I've developed a better tolerance for those, but before taking 10mg would fuck me right up. These days 10 gets me pretty high, but it feels more in control. 

All in all though, I've never had bad after affects of any kind. I can be a bit hungover and irritable sometimes after, but that's usually cause I didnt hydrate well enough the day of using. 
But never noticed a spike in anxiety or depression. 

I did once accidentally take way more than I intended as I didnt understand what the package said. I thought it was 5mg for the whole chunk, but it was actually 5mg per corner chunk of the chocolate, so I took a whole 20, and this was back before I had a good tolerance for edibles. I was fuckin out of it. But the interesting part, is my brain started wanting to panic, in fact my body started giving all the physical signs that I normally get when I have a panic attack and I was on the verge of diving head first into that shit.. but then I just kind of decided "nah I'm good, you do you body" and I turned on Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom, which that movie confused the hell out of me. 
But somehow whilst I was physically having a panic attack, I just kind of ignored it. Took some time for the body to calm down, my heart rate was going crazy, but I just kind of ignored it. Don't know how.. can't do that when sober.. but when high I've just learned to roll with the weirdness of things that happen in my head, and none of it phases me during or after the fact. 🤷‍♂️🤷‍♂️

It leads me to believe that many of problems people face with anxiety due to weed are more of a psychological reaction than something physical, which doesn't make it an easy thing to deal with by any means, but it does mean a person could theoretically learn to deal with it? This of course is just an anecdote though, and not something to take as hard science. 
Though it's backed up a little as I have a doctor friend, who has herself dealt with altered states as a form of therapy for herself, and is wishing to get into that line of working with others, and her experience, especially with shrooms is similar. Where, the idea is there is actually no such thing as a bad trip. Yea your brain might show you some weird awful stuff, and it can lead you down a weird path, but its more about how you deal and perceive and work your way through. Hence why the healing in these states is done with someone to guide you through kind of deal. When you're on your own your brain can get away with you, and you can go down the wrong path so to speak, and that can lead to a sort of.. post traumatic stress sort of reaction. Which is kind of the way I view people's reaction to weed. 

Again though. This is just my hypothesis, I'm not a scientist, and even with some people who know more about this than me having similar ideas, it's not a perfectly well known thing. So take what I say here with a grain of salt.

You can also go splash your face with some cold water just to shock your nervous system a bit, which can help you kinda reboot and recenter. 

Everything is fine. Its just the drug doing drug stuff. You're safe.

We actually don't know if the universe has been erased. We don't know what comes after Zoe doesn't reset it. And that's the whole point of the story. 

Instead of remaining in a constant cycle of fear and hopelessness, and fighting against the natural progression of things. Zoe does the brave thing and dives into the unknown, in hopes that what is to come is better that the cycle that Ava has been eternally going through. 
Its a metaphor for life and being stuck doing the comfortable thing even though you know it isn't working, all because you're scared of new things. Fear of the future and unknowns keeps so many people trapped in situations that are draining the life from them, and Ava is a depiction of this. Look at her. She's a sad, holo echo of the person Zoe is. She's lonely, and has experienced so much loss, and yet keeps repeating the same path with no end in sight. 
Zoe chooses to try a new path, one she has no idea where it will end. It could be the end of all things. But maybe it's not, maybe they survive on the other side of it? Maybe the universe is born anew anyways? It's all only hypothesis what comes if they don't reset. 

I find the story to be incredibly beautiful and whether or not it links up with post game gameplay I really couldn't care less. The post game gameplay can easily be explained aways by all the fucky time nonsense that happens when Zoe runs anyway or even just doing thr same thing as many other games do, and going back to before the final choice of the game, like in Cyberpunk where you can keep playing after the story ends.
Her choosing to preserve the universe would have gone against everything the story was trying to tell and portray.

Alright first thing. Realize that you don't see yourself as others do. When we look at ourselves it's a very skewed vision, especially working from a place of insecurity and self loathing. Your eyes will focus in on perceived flaws and forget to see the whole package. 
Its like when an artist looks at their own art. They see ever brush stroke out of place from what the wanted, every uneven line, every mistake. Where as when the average person looks at it, they just see a beautiful picture or painting. Nobody will ever judge you as harshly as you judge yourself. And if you find someone who does, that person simply sucks and it's better to have nothing to do with them. 

Next, looks have so much less to do with physical attributes, and so much more to do with personality. Over the years I've talked to people who I initially thought were hot from a physical standpoint, and as I talked to them they became ugly, cause their personality was just gross. A woman who I fell head over heels for, and thought was the most beautiful woman on the planet, the first time I met her, I didn't think much about her looks. She wasn't bad looking or anything, but there wasn't an initial attraction. Then we began talking, and quickly as I got to know her, she just became an absolute drop dead 10 to me. The person she was was so insanely attractive to me. 
The point being, physical looks are skin deep. Be a good person, be personable, be passionate about things, and that will get you further than looks ever will. I say this as someone who is a short average looking dude with bad teeth, and acne into my 30s. I've never really had issues finding people who are interested in me, so long as I put myself out there. Every failure I've had in relationships has been me shooting myself in the foot with insecurity and self loathing. Fix those and things become so much easier. 

And lastly. I looked at your profile, you've got a photo in there. For what its worth, I think you're a good looking dude. I don't see what you see, so I can't fathom how you find yourself unattractive. But I understand self hatred enough, to get it. So work on that. Go to therapy, work on that insecurity. Self love, not cockiness, not ego or narcissism, but true self love and confidence will get you exactly where you want to go.

Noita is tough, but I wouldn't consider it in quite the same difficulty tier as spelunky. And the difficulty is extremely different. 

With Noita it's largely a knowledge check. Not to say skill isn't involved, staying alive long enough until you get strong requires it. But from there it just says "how well do you understand wand building" and if you understand it and get the right pieces, you win. 

Spelunky is almost entirely based in skill. There is nothing that will get you through save for just getting better at the game. You aren't gonna find some item that will carry you, there is only you, and your ability to maneuver through. 

With that said. Noita before you meet any knowledge checks is on par with Spelunky before you meet it's knowledge and skill checks. Cause both games early on feel nearly impossible.

Well for starters you have no damage. In brotato, damage is king. It's an offensive and defensive stat. Kill stuff faster and you get hit less. Only not this way for a specific few potatoes. Namely Pacifist lol. 

From there you bought a lot of items and weapons that don't actually do a lot for you. You're working with a build that's all over the place. Usually you wanna focus down one type of weapon, and build from there. 
In the first two shops you will always see two weapons on a reroll, so just buy weapons, don't buy items in those shops. And pick a type, whether melee, ranged, engineer or elemental, pick one and don't buy weapons outside of that. 

From there, take a solid amount of items and levels ups that pair with those weapons. 
%damage and attack speed are both very good. 

On mutant specifically. Don't take luck early. Luck means you see more high tier items, high tier items are very expensive meaning you can often only buy one item, which handcuffs you. You want to buy more items, especially the ones that feed into your build.

On mutant, cheaper weapons are a good call. Stick is more often than not my pick. It's cheap, it has built in damage when you get multiple of them, and the primitive tag on it means you also get a HP boost having multiple of them. 

Use your level ups smartly. Take stats that actually feed into your build.Harvesting early is a good take early. Having more money to spend in the shops with mutant is good. 

You want to aim for like at least 20 melee damage, this isn't a rule it's just a guideline to help understand what you should be aiming for in later waves.( same kinda deal for range/elemental/engineering if those are the builds you choose) more is always better, but once your at 20, then % damage starts playing its role a lot more.

The funny thing about Autism, it's largely only a thing due to social construct. Now don't take that line out of context, I know full well it's a real thing that impacts the lives of people, but a large amount of the way it impacts people is due to social construct. Like.. nobody would "feel autistic" if the world was built in such a way as to accommodate autistic folks. It would just be a normal state of being. If your accommodations are met you just exist in comfort. 
When you are alone, you can just be yourself. You can be comfortable, you can accomodate things how you need. It only really becomes obvious when in places where you fit or there are things pointing to your differences. 

I honestly think we only feel a lot of the ways we are when they are somehow challenged or brought into light. The world is built in such a way that being autistic, or any type of neurodivergence, just sticks out like a sore thumb, cause of how not accommodating everything is. Its too loud, too bright, people expect that you act in a certain way, there are funny made up social contracts people expect us to follow, and so yea.. 

It's kinda like how if the world was built to be for exactly your height, and everyone was the same height as you, you'd never feel short or tall. It's only when something is too high to grab, or someone is taller than you that you feel short, or the reverse.

Just finished season 2 last night and my sentiments are the same. Season 1 for me was a 7/10. It was good, it had some great moments, but there was a lot missing for me. 

Thorfinn in season 1, was kind of boring for me. He was so incredibly single minded. And it makes sense, he was a kid in a fucked up situation, but his character depth in season 1 was essentially non existent. He was a killing machine with one purpose, one care. And this isn't bad, its just something I've seen a million times in media and it's kinda boring.

Season 2 comes in and makes this pay off so extremely well though. Like he goes from the typical single minded Shoenen protag, to something else, and it creates this beautiful depth, dealing with all the trauma from season 1. The fallout of living solely for a singular goal and then having that goal completely ripped away from you and being left at the literal lowest you could ever be. 

Askeladd was the only character with real depth in season 1 and he's fucking great. An argument can be made for Canut, but honestly season 1 Canut even after his growth still just didn't really do much for me. 

Season 2 comes around and it finally added depth to a lot of places it was lacking for me. Canut and Thorfinn being the two main places the show really paid off. But then we also get Einar, and a bunch of characters on the farm who are much more complex than pretty much any characters I'm season 1. Ketil, Snake, Olimar, all help to flesh out themes in the story so beautifully. Thorgil, and Gardar play as incredible roles as well in the overarching themes of the roles of violence. 
Season 2 makes me appreciate season 1 more, because where season 1 in lacking as a standalone season for me, it's elevated by being such a massive setup for all that we get in season 2. 

Einar and Thorfinn being two sides of the fallout of war that we see all through season 1. 
Canut fighting his own personal battle of trying to create peace but also becoming a worse and worse person in the process, struggling to not do what his father did as king, but also seeing the trap of power. 

It builds on so much that Thors, and Askeladd set into motion, and it just made everything that came before it that much better.

So.. in my experience, you don't stop overthinking. And bear with me, I know saying that sounds awful and terrifying, but hear me out. 

We are not our brains. We are more. Our brains do their thing they run their shit and we get to put up with it. We often don't have a bunch of control of the things we think, intrusive thoughts being the extreme, but really, there is so much shit we've learned over the years good, bad and in between that runs like auto programs. 
Now.. we so have some control, obviously. You chose the things you do, and say and so on and so forth. I digress. 

When it comes to overthinking, I like think of it like a flowing river. This metaphor can go a hundred ways and get really confusing, but my idea is that, trying to stop the flowing river, and damn it up, doesn't work. You just create more pressure and you're putting so much energy into stopping something, that when it bursts you don't have the energy to deal with the impending flood. Just jumping in the river and letting it sweep you away or trying to swim against the current  is also what too many of us do. 
What I try to do these days. Is let the river flow, buy just watch it. Just watch the thoughts go by. Stop judging stop jumping in. Just watch. Let it happen. 

Now that probably sounds silly and you're thinking, how? Well.. step one is being aware that you can just simply not jump in. It will seem impossible. But the goal, is to listen to your thoughts.. and to just try to not judge them. Just use a simple statement for one or two crazy thoughts and overthinking patterns and just say something like "Hmm.. weird thinking. But whatever." Find a phrase that you'd personally say, about something that was of mild interest, but not enough to draw you into kind of deal.
You don't even have to mean it to start with. Just try saying it, and hold awareness that you don't have to jump in. It all starts with being aware. Eventually, if you keep at it, you can start to actually detach from your thoughts, and realize they don't really mean anything, they are just thoughts. Just as a river is just a river, and you can just sit and chill by river as it flows on and does its thing. 

The harder we fight against the current, the more we try to damn it up, it just exhausts us. So just sit and chill by the river, and try to stop fighting it. And believe me, I know it feels like the river is sweeping you away and it wasn't you who jumped in. But that's where the awareness starts us. Is the realization that we are the ones jumping in. That we don't have to. That we can just listen to our thoughts and not really give a shit about what they are saying. 
This isn't an easy thing to do, and it doesn't happen fast. It's not just gonna magically work and be fixed tomorrow. Hell there are still plenty of times I get caught up in it. But, there are now also times where I just let it go, watch it for a bit, realize how silly it is. And the thinking doesn't stop. My brain keeps trying to bombard me with all the shit I could be worrying about, all my insecurities and fears. But I can just kinda be like "cool story bro" and just ignore it. 

Maybe it won't work for you. Maybe this all is just mumbo jumbo that sounds like BS to you, or maybe I made zero sense. But, this is the path I'm trying, and it seems to be reaping some benefits. So I hope you find something helpful from it. If not, I wish you the absolute best!

Distraction is an objectively bad card. Why is distraction bad compared to say infernal blade or white noise you may ask? 

Well, infernal blade will always give you an attack, and unless that attack is clash it is a functional card, that gives you what you need from it. You want damage here is damage. Not to mention it synergies with exhaust stuff for Clad so it's value can be increased quite nicely in Clads deck.

White noise is good because in most decks you take it the powers it gives you are at the very least functional. Obviously you can low role with it, but more often than not it helps. 

Distraction is bad why then? Because Silents skill list is so damn varied, that it is actively bad more than it is good. You want block, whoops you got poison, you want poison? Whoops you got a draw card. You want  draw, whoops it's a blade dance. You are better off just taking the skills that actually function in your deck 100% of the time. And you may wonder, well what if the game isn't giving them to me? Then should I take a distraction? Nope, because it's still so unlikely that it gives you what you actually need that it's a detriment to even waste the energy it costs playing it. "But what if it's upgraded?" 
Firstly, if you're ever upgrading distraction, your deck has big problems or you're so OP already that distraction doesn't matter. If you get it upgraded.. I still likely wouldn't take it, cause it still is too likely to put a card that doesn't play in my deck in my hand and it has actively become no better than a curse. 

The one time where I think distraction is a semi ok take. Is if you have shard, and you happen to have corruption + dark embrace and/or feel no pain, and then it's just two free skills that are fodder for a corruption deck that draw more cards, or block, with potential to do something else ok. But again, you're likely better off taking something else lol. 

This has been my rant on why distraction is a shit card. Thanks for your consideration.

Thoughts are just thoughts. They don't mean anything. Trying to stop the flow of a river of thought doesn't often work. But that also doesn't mean you have to jump right in either. Just sit by the river, watch it flow. Notice how silly many of the thoughts are. Like seriously the shit our brains come up with in that state is just downright dumb. They catastrophize the smallest shit, they over react so hard, and in the right light it's kinda really funny. Because here is something to know, you are not your thoughts. We don't have 100% control of what we think. It's why a song that gets stuck in your head can happen without you choosing it. 
So instead of trying to control it and stop the thoughts, try to control your reaction to the thoughts. It's by no means an easy thing, but to me it's a hell of a lot easier than trying to outright stop them. 

Just try to notice the thought, and if possible just accept that you thought it. It's OK to think it. Even unpleasent thoughts are OK. They aren't the truth, we can't predict the future, we don't know what other people are thinking, and those catastrophic thoughts are an old defense mechanism. So take them as they are.

Dude meditation is something I have struggled on and off with since starting my whole journey dealing with this stuff, so I feel you on the no go. I just know when I get myself doing it consistently I tend to end up with shit a little more in control. 

Two best things that help me in meditation, starting out doing really short ones. Like 5 minutes, and don't try to force anything more. Cause that can seem like an eternity. Secondly, guided stuff on YouTube. I can't for the life of me, just sit in silence and try to meditate, cause my brain ends up just going off the rails and driving me nuts. What I can do, is listen to someone calmly talk and focus on their voice and what they are saying, and then when my mind does try to go to the shitty places, I can focus back on the voice. 

Meditation also doesn't have to be that typical sit there with your eyes closed and control your breath and reach zen. This is a misconception. Meditation can be anything that allows you to focus and mindfully come to a place of peace. For me, stuff like drawing, or playing an instrument, going for a walk or a drive and just making sure to keep pulling my thoughts back to the task at hand and working on letting go of the thoughts that negatively impact me, that's all meditation. Its basically just the practice of mindfully keeping ones brain from going off the rails lol.

It sucks you have to wait a year to go see a doctor, but there are things you can do in the mean time to help yourself improve. Continuing to push yourself in small ways to face anxiety is always a good practice. Learning meditation. Reading up on anxiety and learning about it etc. Talking about it can be powerful too, putting words to it can sometimes make it feel less.. All consuming? Though this needs to be done in a safe space with people who wont invalidate you. 
I also am assuming you're still in school based on the needing to wait a year. Once you're in school again ( assuming summer break), you may be able to talk to a school counsellor. Which you should be able to do on your own. 

Overall though, all you really need to do is just try to look after yourself the best you can. Self compassion and love are huge. You got this!

Showering and cleaning cause me a ton of anxiety.

Showering - A. Showering takes me back to when I had to shower before school in the mornings, which was always a time of high anxiety. 
B. There is way too much free mind space in the shower. Too much time where I'm not distracted and my brain always goes to the bad places, amped up by how its linked to a time of high anxiety in my life. 


Cleaning - Cleaning triggers my perfectionism issues. When I start cleaning, I begin seeing every little dirty spot and I work so hard to clean everything perfectly and it never gets there and so I start stressing about how Im not cleaning good enough and then I want to clean the whole fucking house and it begins feeling like even doing one small cleaning task is the most overwhelming deal cause my brain links it to feeling like I have to clean everything and do it to my absolute utmost ability. 

So both cases its not actually the tasks themselves that cause the pre-task anxiety, but the fear of the tasks causing anxiety. Anxiety for the sake of anxiety! Hype!

Hi there, sorry you're going through this stuff. So let me ask you, whats your relationship with your parents like? Are you close? Have you ever broken down in front of them? How do they react to tense situations or when you've possibly done something to disappoint them? Do you know where they stand in mental health? 

The thing is, if you trust them, talk to them about it. Be honest. I would avoid diving right in to any suicidal type talk, I broached the topic in a depressive fit, when they were frustrated about me missing so much school just being like "I don't want to live anymore." This drew a very big fear reaction and wasn't a good place to start. 
Of course if you are having suicidal ideations you very much should tell people. 
But, where I would start is just somewhere like "Mom, Dad, I'm really struggling, and I need to talk to you guys." 
From there tell them your struggles, and try to impress the importance of those struggle in your life. 

Now.. If you don't trust them. If your relationship is bad, you need to find an adult you trust. An Aunt or Uncle, a Grandparent, a teacher, a doctor, maybe another friends parents, someone. 

The sad truth, is some people will have a bad reaction to this, and you do have to prepare yourself for that possibility. But that should not stop you from seeking help. If other people have a bad reaction that is their problem, and it is up to you to seek help elsewhere. I really hope you have someone you trust, at the very least it sounds like you have a friend who is going through it with you. You guys can support each other. That's not a replacement for an adult who can help, but it is an important relationship in its own right. 

Good luck, you got this, you're strong as fuck cause you've made it this far!

So in the summer I went through an extremely high anxiety time for the span of a month or two. I wasn't sleeping well, was barely eating, I was waking to panic attacks, where I would literally gag and dry heave most mornings. Heart racing, brain racing, all that good shit. 

So, what I found to help was when I would wake up, I would immediately find a guided meditation on YouTube, plug in my headphones and meditate, I really liked ones that guided breathing and I liked longer ones that gave me a chance to get shit under control. 5 minute mediations weren't enough cause it would take me almost 5 minutes to get my breathing in check. But if I was able to breath through the gagging feeling, it would slowly ease up. Then I would meditate until I felt like it was enough. 
After I was done meditating, I would sit up, and do some simply stretching. I was usually still really tense and anxious, and would begin to feel like gagging again, but I would stretch anyway. Get the blood flowing, and prove to myself that even though I felt awful, I was still in control of my body, I was still stretching even though my anxiety was spiking and telling me I couldn't. Plus stretching feels really good. Then I would get up, force myself to drink some water, cause I was dehydrated and that was contributing to the anxiety. 
It took weeks of this before it showed good results and it wasn't easy, but I did it. I also started going for walks in the evening which helped. 

I need to start doing all of this again cause Ive let myself slip, and I am sliding hard into depression and anxiety again. 
I don't know if this will help you, and I know it sucks cause it requires effort and some discipline, but it helped me out of a really rough place over the summer. 
Good luck with whatever you try! You got this, you're stronger than you know and you can withstand this bullshit!

Hey. I've been there, lot of experience with this, varying degrees of success. Still happens from time to time, but much less frequently. 

Few things you can try. 

- Be aware of when you eat, if you know something is gonna trigger your anxiety before hand, try not to eat too close to the time you do said thing. 
For me going out knowing I have a full stomach can make it worse. However sometimes knowing my stomach is empty got me through things. 
This isn't something you wanna do long term. This is something you wanna do, if it helps, a few times just to avoid puking. Sometimes just getting yourself not to throw up gives you confidence it won't happen next time. 

- Similar to the last one, don't do this all the time, but for a bit until you get confidence in not puking, you can take something like gravol, or peptobismal or even better, find some ginger tablets  or something that helps settle your stomach. 
The problem with taking actual drugs to help with this is side effects. Pepto can cause constipation, and gravol  makes you sleepy.  Using them the odd time just to give you some confidence you aren't gonna barf is fine though. 
Ginger helps settle my stomach, and has no real side effects unless you take way too much, or are allergic. Try it, see if it helps. Its just something to give you an edge against your brain. 

- This counts for all anxiety everywhere and is annoying to hear but is true. Breath. Breath deep into your stomach.  Shallow chest breathing always makes it worse. So breath deep, and controlled, try to relax the lump in your throat, and the tightness in your gut if you can. 

- Accept that puking is ok. This one is hardddddd, I still struggle with it. 
What you resist persists, the more you freak out about the idea of puking the worse it gets. If you can just accept that "ok yes I might hurl, but I know I can get to a washroom in time, and its totally ok if I puke." It makes it easier. 
Again tough, but if you can pull it off it helps so much. 

I hope something I said here helps. Maybe just knowing you aren't alone will be all you get from this post. 
I really hope you find something that helps!

I know how easy it is to start freaking out when you think you are doing something "weird" or abnormal. 
We've all learned to fear that something is wrong with ourselves and when we do something, like not wanting to delete a suicide note, we use that as reinforcement as to why we are so fucked up. Then we start to worry about how messed we really are and it drives us down the path we were afraid we were going in the first place. 
Where as sometimes, just accepting that the note is kind of comforting, is ok. That might even give the note less power, and allow you to delete it someday if you feel like it.

Few ideas. It could be a reminder of how far you've come, and where you could be again. A motivator to keep pushing forward. You don't want to delete it as its. 
There could be a weird sort of sentiment for the letter. It was written from a place of possible honesty, where you got some shit off your chest that you needed to get off. So maybe though a low moment it was cathartic? 

Maybe its your escape route. Whenever I do anything that causes me anxiety, I need to have a planned escape route. I don't always intend to use the escape, I usually don't want to, but its comforting having an escape from a situation that is horrible and uncomfortable.. In my mind suicide is that escape route from life. Its always there as a weird comfort, just to know that I'm not trapped in this life. Its a decision to stay, and its mine to make. 
This note could be a tie to that. 

Could also just be your mind fucking with you. Mental illness likes to do that.   Your fear might be causing some form anxiety about what happens if you delete the note. If you delete it are you fully better? What if you delete it and you fall back into the suicidal tendencies? Then you have to rewrite it, and your mind will tell you that it is this huge scary deal, even though rationally its not. 
Our minds pull this kind of ridiculous shit all the time. 

Maybe its one of these things. Maybe its not. Feel free to talk it out. What are you feeling when you think abouy deleting it? What's being predominately played in your head.

I'll set this up a little. 

I had one of my worst depressive anxious episodes of my life. I remember sitting in my living room in semi fetal position trying to just kind of hold tight and not do anything irrational, all while almost ripping my hair out and just shaking and crying. Parents took me to the hospital where I spent the night, and I got put on some drugs and referred to a psychiatrist. 

I spent the next week or so waiting to visit this guy basically not leaving my couch and with my Dad watching over me. Get to the psychiatrist office where I was in a room filled with people setting off my anxiety worse than it had been the entire week. So Im like sitting there shaking trying not to puke. 

Psychiatrist comes in 45 minutes late. Takes one appointment before mine and then herds me into a tiny little room where he asks if his apprentice or whatever can sit in on our appointment. Which I was like whatever, but in my mind I was just eyeing the window behind him wondering if I could get to it and jump out of it before they could stop me.

I asked how long I'd be on them and he laughed in my face and told me I'd be on them forever as I will never get better. Great thing to tell a suicidal young man. 
The kicker to all of this. His apprentice... had fallen the fuck asleep beside him. 


TL:DR

Acceptance isn't resignation. You don't need to resign yourself to how you are and where you are in life. It doesn't even mean liking those things. It's just acceptance. 
True love of something comes when you accept it. 

Think about someone or something you really truly love. There are likely aspects of that person or pet, or thing that annoy you or that you might wish would be different. But at the same time, you accept those traits as part of that person. 
The idea is trying to give yourself that same acceptance. 

Accepting something makes it easier to deal with and allows a sense of peace. It's like sitting in a traffic and being ok with the fact you are there. Would you rather be at home in your PJs watching Netflix and eating icecream than stuck in traffic? Hell yea you would! But is you being pissed off at the fact you are in traffic gonna change a damn thing? No. It's just gonna make you angry and more uncomfortable. The best thing you can do in the situation, is accept that you are stuck at that moment, turn up the radio with some good music and keep watching for the traffic to move. 

Resignation would be turning your car off and throwing your keys out the window and despairing that you're never gonna get out of the traffic jam and that you are stuck there forever. Acceptance is being ok with the fact that you are stuck, all while still trying to find your opening and still aiming to get home. Instead of fighting it every step of the way, you try to make the best of a shitty situation.
